title: In 2009, Brian Acton applied for a job at Facebook and was rejected. He had already been turned down
description:
In 2009, Brian Acton applied for a job at Facebook and was rejected. He had already been turned down by Twitter too. He was an experienced engineer, not a novice: both companies passed on him within the same year.

He tweeted about the Facebook rejection on 3 August 2009: 'Facebook turned me down. It was a great opportunity to connect with some fantastic people. Looking forward to life's next adventure.' His next adventure was already underway. Former Yahoo colleague Jan Koum had incorporated WhatsApp Inc. that February, and Acton joined him later that year.

Acton helped raise 250,000 dollars in seed funding from five former Yahoo colleagues and was granted co-founder status once he came aboard. The money came from people who already trusted him from his Yahoo days, not from a venture pitch to strangers.

roughly the value, in dollars, of the deal Facebook announced on 19 February 2014 to acquire WhatsApp, the company built by the man it had rejected for a job.

The deal, split between cash, stock and restricted stock units, closed on 6 October 2014, eight months after the announcement.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Acton: confirms Brian Acton was rejected for a job at Facebook in 2009, having earlier also been turned down by Twitter, and that he later co-founded WhatsApp with former Yahoo colleague Jan Koum, going on to raise seed funding from other former Yahoo colleagues and receive co-founder status.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WhatsApp: confirms Jan Koum incorporated WhatsApp Inc. in California on 24 February 2009, that Brian Acton joined him later that year and helped raise 250,000 dollars in seed funding from five former Yahoo colleagues, and that Facebook announced its acquisition of WhatsApp on 19 February 2014 for a deal valued at approximately 19.3 billion dollars in cash, stock and restricted stock units, which closed on 6 October 2014.
